security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are parser artifacts caused by Go import blocks, Markdown code spans, documentation links, and browser configuration values. The dependency setup command is a confirmed medium risk because it runs an unpinned remote Go package and installs system dependencies. The main concern is explicit guidance for bypassing anti-bot controls through stealth and human-emulation techniques.

remediation.issue: The skill directs agents to bypass anti-bot systems with stealth techniques, proxy rotation, and simulated human behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evasion instructions and limit automation guidance to authorized testing, documented APIs, and site terms.

remediation.issue: The installation command executes the latest remote Playwright Go installer and may add system dependencies.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed module version and require user confirmation before installing browsers or operating-system packages.

content.user_title: Build Reliable Browser Automation in Go
content.value_statement: Dynamic websites are difficult to test and automate reliably with basic HTTP tools. This skill guides Playwright Go architecture, logging, cleanup, timeouts, and browser interactions.
actual_capabilities: Structures Playwright Go programs around one browser and isolated contexts.
Adds Zap logging for navigation, interaction, and error events.
Applies explicit timeouts, panic recovery, and deferred cleanup.
Provides examples for initialization, typing, clicking, and session persistence.
Supports debugging with visible browsers and slowed interactions.
limitations: Requires Playwright drivers, browser binaries, and Go dependencies.
Full browser automation can consume substantial memory and processor capacity.
Examples omit complete cookie serialization and restoration code.
The skill does not solve CAPTCHAs or guarantee access to protected sites.

use_cases.title: Test Dynamic Web Applications
use_cases.description: Create repeatable browser tests for navigation, forms, and JavaScript-rendered interfaces.

use_cases.title: Automate Internal Browser Workflows
use_cases.description: Build authorized browser tasks with isolated sessions, structured logs, and reliable cleanup.

use_cases.title: Debug Playwright Go Scripts
use_cases.description: Review failing automation and add visible execution, timeouts, error handling, and diagnostics.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Browser Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Playwright Go test for [URL] that verifies [expected result]. Use explicit timeouts and close all resources.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one authorized test flow.

prompt_templates.title: Add Structured Logging
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this Playwright Go workflow to use Zap logging for navigation, clicks, failures, and cleanup: [workflow].
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve observability in an existing automation.

prompt_templates.title: Design Concurrent Sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Playwright Go service for [session count] isolated sessions using one browser. Include lifecycle management, limits, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a Production Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this authorized Playwright Go workflow: [workflow]. Address timeouts, retries, logging privacy, session isolation, dependency pinning, and graceful shutdown.

output_examples.input: Create a browser test for a dashboard login and page heading.
output_examples.output: A Go test outline that launches Chromium, creates an isolated context, performs the login, checks the heading, logs failures, and closes resources.

output_examples.input: Improve a script that opens a new browser for every task.
output_examples.output: A refactoring plan that keeps one browser, creates a context per task, limits concurrency, and centralizes cleanup and error reporting.

output_examples.input: Diagnose intermittent click failures in a Playwright Go workflow.
output_examples.output: A review identifying selector readiness, explicit timeout, visibility, logging, and debug-mode checks, followed by targeted correction steps.

best_practices: Use one browser with separate contexts for independent sessions.
Set explicit timeouts and close pages, contexts, browsers, and Playwright.
Pin dependencies and protect credentials, cookies, and form values in logs.
anti_patterns: Do not launch a new browser process for every small task.
Do not ignore Playwright errors or depend only on default timeouts.
Do not use stealth techniques to bypass access controls or site policies.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It provides Playwright Go architecture, examples, and review guidance for browser automation and testing.

faq.question: Does it install Playwright automatically?
faq.answer: No. Installation requires a separate command that downloads browser components and may install system dependencies.

faq.question: Can it test JavaScript applications?
faq.answer: Yes. Playwright runs a real browser and can interact with JavaScript-rendered pages.

faq.question: Does it support multiple sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends one browser with separate contexts for isolated cookies, cache, and storage.

faq.question: Can it solve CAPTCHAs?
faq.answer: No. The skill does not provide CAPTCHA solving capabilities.

faq.question: Is protected-site automation appropriate?
faq.answer: Only automate systems you are authorized to access. Follow site terms, published APIs, rate limits, and applicable law.
